query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a hybrid thermo-mechanical processing route—specifically, severe cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling—will refine the dual-phase lamellar microstructure of eutectic high-entropy alloys, resulting in a heterogeneous nanostructure that simultaneously increases room-temperature strength and tensile ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) in the as-cast state with dual-phase lamellar colonies possessing extensive internal boundaries.
generation.intervention: Hybrid rolling consisting of an initial severe cryo-rolling step to store deformation energy and induce microstructural refinement, followed by warm-rolling to promote controlled dynamic recrystallization.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature tensile deformation; processing parameters (e.g., reduction in thickness, rolling temperatures) similar to those used in referenced studies on AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA.
generation.structural_mediator: A heterogeneous nanostructured lamellar colony featuring a mix of ultrafine recrystallized regions and coarser, recovered regions that act to impede crack initiation and propagation.
generation.mechanism: The cryo-rolling step introduces significant stored energy and refines the microstructure, while the subsequent warm-rolling exploits this energy to accelerate controlled recrystallization without coarsening. This results in a microstructure that enhances strength by grain refinement and ductility by promoting crack deflection and intrinsic toughening mechanisms at the phase boundaries.
generation.predicted_outcome: Tensile tests at room temperature will show increased yield and ultimate tensile strengths along with improved elongation to failure compared to samples processed by conventional methods.
generation.baseline: Conventional processing routes (e.g., standard casting and simple thermo-mechanical processing) that typically produce lamellar colonies with limited tensile ductility and lower strength.
generation.boundary: The benefits are expected to be effective for eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar structures similar to AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and may not translate to single-phase HEAs or alloys with significantly different microstructures.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of strength and ductility improvements is uncertain, and optimization might be required for different alloys or processing parameters. Additionally, the robustness of the microstructural benefits under various loading conditions beyond quasi-static tensile tests needs further exploration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA samples: one processed via the hybrid rolling (cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling) route and one via conventional processing. Subject both sets to identical room-temperature tensile tests. Characterize the microstructure of each sample using SEM/TEM to correlate mechanical properties with microstructural features.
measurements: Grain size and phase distribution from microstructural analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hybrid-rolled samples do not show statistically significant improvements in both tensile strength and ductility compared to the conventional processing baseline, or if the microstructural characterization fails to reveal the formation of a heterogeneous nanostructured lamellar colony, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
proposed by Lu et al., are a special class of HEAs having promising mechanical properties in the as-cast condition. In particular, the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 nano-lamellar EHEA consisting of soft L12/FCC and hard B2 phases has attracted considerable attention due to their attractive mechanical properties over a wide temperature range, and ample opportunities for further tailoring their microstructure and properties by thermo-mechanical processing (TMP),. Bhattacharjee et al. showed that heavily cryo-rolled and annealed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA develops a complex heterogeneous microstructure consisting of retained lamellar and coarse non-lamellar regions. The individual domains again consisted of multiscale architecture ranging from ultrafine recrystallized FCC grains to coarse recovered B2 grains, which resulted in simultaneous enhancement in strength and ductility. Shi et al. have shown that the properties of the EHEA can be further improved by tuning the inherited lamellar microstructure of the EHEA.
